study.question: After the pivot-chart plus sign representation failed to recover signed-model quality, can a target-relative chart make coarse orientation learnable at unchanged active parameter capacity, or is the loss insensitive to this reference choice?
study.hypothesis: Observed g1-r0068-axis_with_sign AUC 0.6664435963 versus axis_constant 0.6664137638 shows only +0.0000298325 recovery; signed_with_sign 0.6683550095 versus signed_constant 0.6684153206 gives -0.0000603112, interaction +0.0000901437. Thus informational sufficiency of (c,s), with c=s*m, did not imply one-pass learnability. A provisional mechanism is that the max-absolute-coordinate sign has a difficult relation to the target and a moving embedding chart. Orienting the same coarse vector by its dot product with the already-supplied current item may make the sign scalar directly relevant to target-relative trend. A target-chart x sign-availability factorial can distinguish a selective scalar benefit from a chart-only optimization benefit. This is an untested local follow-up, not a novelty claim or an assertion of useful whole-sequence order.

study.proposed_difference: Cross coarse_chart_reference in {target,pivot} with expose_coarse_sign in {true,false}. Let m be the original masked coarse vector, q the existing target embedding over item fields, and p its original pivot sign. Compute d=<m_item,q> and a=||m_item||*||q|| in FP32 on detached tensors. If |d|>1e-6*a, use s=sign(d), otherwise s=p; zero pivot is +1 and ties use the first max-absolute coordinate. Target chart c=s*m includes all historical action coordinates but the inner product has no current-action coordinate. The pivot chart is unchanged. Append s or constant +1 to BOTH existing learned consumers while passing the selected c into the existing coarse slot. Each cell computes both charts. There is no explicit multiplicative decoder restoring m for the learned consumers. At fixed q, c(-m)=c(m) and s*c=m, including fallback cases; no event permutation or new information is introduced.
predictions: Primary screening prediction: target_with_sign improves over pivot_with_sign by at least 0.0005 click AUC, target_with_sign minus target_constant is at least 0.0005, and interaction I=(T1-T0)-(P1-P0) is at least 0.0005. These are predeclared practical effect thresholds, not significance tests.

Strong recovery prediction: target_with_sign is within 0.0005 click AUC of existing g1-r0068-signed_constant (0.6684153206), subject to successful pivot bridges. The unchanged g0-r0052-block_nonlinear_transfer (0.6685268680) remains the utility control and current best measured model.

Pivot_with_sign and pivot_constant should reproduce g1-r0068-axis_with_sign and g1-r0068-axis_constant within 0.0001 AUC each; larger drift suspends across-round recovery claims pending source/native parity audit. These same-seed bridges are not independent repetitions.

If target_constant improves similarly to target_with_sign and I stays small, the result favors a reference/optimization explanation over selective orientation-bit utility. Target-relative bit usefulness would still concern this summary under retained order channels, not causal sequence order or full content-only invariance.
falsifiers: Any native validity/masking/source-gradient/buffer/initialization parity failure invalidates comparisons until corrected; it is an implementation failure, not scientific counterevidence.

With valid stable bridges, I below 0.0005 or target_with_sign gain over target_constant below 0.0005 fails the predicted selective rescue in this one-pass setting; do not claim mechanism support from a tiny positive fluctuation.

If target_with_sign remains more than 0.0005 below the signed control, target-relative sign exposure has not recovered signed quality, even if it beats pivot charts. This does not prove coarse sign intrinsically necessary or information insufficient.
An apparent gain that does not recur on paired additional seeds, or violates the cost reserve/cap, cannot support repeated or efficient improvement.

Target anchor is a learned embedding and may drift; chart switches can affect optimization and upstream gradients
Both charts remove only global sign of one coarse summary; other order-sensitive channels remain
Equal parameter counts and matched source paths do not establish equal measured cost or an equal-compute frontier
Scalar restoration requires nonlinear cross-feature decoding; the fixed-width one-pass consumers may fail for either reference
Target dot products may be near zero so pivot fallback dominates; a null result would then weakly test target orientation. Log margin/fallback frequency only if authorized charged diagnostics exist
Target and history embed missing/special IDs under the inherited benchmark; target-reference signs could reflect that representation rather than useful preference evolution
Native precision/reduction behavior, batch normalization trajectory, learned-target chart switching, or sign-boundary frequency could change training without a new predictive signal
